sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• Season 1 runner-up: madlabs, Bl4zeDaddy and DrewAJC lost the Final to Lawson State.
  • madlabs returns as captain; both teammates left to manage their own clubs — Bl4zeDaddy to Own Goal FC, DrewAJC to Bucky Irving FC. 999 is the only club that lost two players to rival managerships.
  • Roster: madlabs (captain, $8,041), Killua ($5,590), on rollr ($4,366). $5,746 left on the cap — the most unspent of any team.
  • Rebuilt entirely with players new to RPL.

sections.heading: Season 1
sections.html: madlabs finished Season 1 with one of the league's most balanced stat lines — 399.85 avg points, 3rd-highest, across 26 games — on the team that reached the Final. Both of the players he lost to rival clubs were developed on that roster.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
The only club that consistently bought below model value. Killua cost $5,590 against a Champion I rank baseline of $8,655 — a ~35% discount on a player seeded at the second-highest rank tier in the league. on rollr cost $4,366 against a $4,845 baseline, a smaller discount.

madlabs finished with $5,746 unspent, more than any other manager, while assembling a roster whose rank profile is higher than its price. Whether that's disciplined value-hunting or a cap he never found a use for is the open question — and it's the mirror image of Lawson State's approach in the same auction.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html: The most conservative spend in the league, on the least-measured roster. Killua and on rollr have no RPL games on record, so both of their valuations are rank-seeded rather than earned. If the Champion I seed on Killua reflects real ability, 999 got the best value in the draft. If it doesn't, madlabs is carrying two unknowns and $5,746 he can no longer spend, since rosters locked at the end of the draft.

sections.heading: Season 2 — no games played yet
sections.html: 999 was on bye for Match Day 1 and has yet to play a Season 2 series. Killua and on rollr have no player profiles yet for the same reason.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• New club for Season 2, built by DrewAJC in his first season as a manager. He played on 999 in Season 1 alongside madlabs and Bl4zeDaddy.
  • Roster: DrewAJC (captain, $3,063), Blockymalrd ($8,091), drateRbmud ($7,000). $5,589 left on the cap.
  • The league's only all-veteran, zero-rookie roster — every player has Season 1 experience.
  • Named Fire Water Gang at auction time and renamed to Bucky Irving FC after the draft completed.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
DrewAJC was the lowest-valued captain at $3,063, which under the fixed lowest-to-highest nomination order meant he nominated first in every round — first pick of the board, every time.

He used it to buy experience at a premium. Blockymalrd cost $8,091 against a Season 1 model value of $3,970 (a ~2.0× premium) and drateRbmud cost $7,000 against $4,168 (~1.7×). Both gaps are large and neither is explained by the stats alone: Blockymalrd finished Season 1 as a mid-pack Diamond II, and drateRbmud a mid-pack Diamond I.

He still finished with $5,589 unspent, the second-most in the league.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html: A roster assembled on a thesis the stats don't directly support — that Season 1 experience is worth paying above model for. It's the most testable bet in the league, because the counter-example is sitting right there: Fortnite Flick FC's all-rookie roster beat them on Match Day 1.

sections.heading: Season 2 — Match Day 1 (2026-09-02)
sections.html:
Lost 1–2 to Fortnite Flick FC. 6 goals for, 11 against.

The result and the underlying numbers point in opposite directions, and it's the sharpest example of that gap on the match day. Bucky Irving won almost every resource battle: most boost collected of any team (23,205), most stolen (4,316), highest boost BPM (418, i.e. the busiest team on the field), and a lopsided 12-to-1 demo count in their favour. All of that physical dominance produced one series win out of three games.

drateRbmud justified his price — 4 goals across the series, including a 2-goal Game 2 that levelled it. Blockymalrd scored twice and inflicted a league-high 8 demos on the day. But DrewAJC, the manager who bet everything on veteran chemistry, didn't score once in three games — 0 goals on 0.0% shooting.

Whether the gap between activity and results closes as the roster settles, or whether it's a real finishing problem, is the thing to watch.

Territorial and boost figures are ballchasing.com proxies, not literal possession.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• New club for Season 2, built by F1yTe Bacon — himself new to RPL, and the only manager who is both a first-time manager and a first-time player.
  • Roster: F1yTe Bacon (captain, $8,655), Jart ($12,689), Ugadawg50 ($900). $1,499 left on the cap.
  • Holds the widest price spread on any single roster in league history: $12,689 to $900.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
Jart at $12,689 was the most expensive non-captain purchase of the entire auction — against a rank-seeded baseline of $8,655, since he was new to RPL with no Season 1 record. A ~1.5× premium on a player with no league history at all.

Ugadawg50 at $900 is the cheapest purchase in RPL auction history. He carried no Season 1 Player Value because TTT was pulled from competition, and his raw numbers over 7 games (142.86 avg points) were the weakest recorded per-game production in league history.

Nearly 60% of the cap went into two players, one of whom had never played an RPL game.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html: The highest-variance roster in the league. Both the record signing and the record bargain were bets on unmeasured players — Jart had no RPL history, Ugadawg50's history was voided. Only F1yTe Bacon's own valuation rests on anything, and that's rank-seeded too.

sections.heading: Season 2 — Match Day 1 (2026-09-02)
sections.html:
Swept 0–3 by Own Goal FC. 5 goals for, 11 against.

A rough opening night in every dimension, not just the scoreline. California Gurls spent the most time at 0 boost of any team (583.5 seconds — boost-starved more than anyone), the least time in the attacking third (14.7%), and stole the fewest boost (1,936). They lost the territorial and resource battle as clearly as they lost the games.

F1yTe Bacon was the one bright spot: 2 goals, 2 assists and 5 saves across the sweep, present in all three losses without getting much help. Jart, the record signing, contributed goals and assists but recorded zero saves across the series. Ugadawg50 had the single lowest individual game of the night — a 74 score in Game 1 — on his way to an 0–3 series, which tracks with the Season 1 note already on his file.

One match day, and it was against the best team on the night. But nothing here yet contradicts the pre-season read.

Territorial figures are ballchasing.com proxies, not literal possession.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• New club for Season 2, and the league's only all-rookie roster — LLellum, Sajar47 and TRS 1000 had never played an RPL game before Match Day 1.
  • Roster: LLellum (captain, $15,000), Sajar47 ($5,719), TRS 1000 ($2,400). $624 left on the cap — the tightest of any team.
  • Built around LLellum, a Grand Champion I and the highest-ranked player in league history, well above the previous ceiling.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
LLellum's $15,000 is an outlier in the most literal sense: it's above the $10,000 maximum the value model can normally produce, and he's handled as an Exempt case rather than through the usual valuation path. Auto-drafting him consumed nearly two-thirds of the cap before the auction started.

That left $8,743 for two players, and the results diverged sharply from model expectations. Sajar47 went for $5,719 against a $5,705 rank-seeded baseline — almost exactly at model. TRS 1000 went for $2,400 against a $4,845 baseline, roughly half price, the largest discount of the entire auction.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html: The most top-heavy roster in the league by a wide margin, and — going into Match Day 1 — the one with the least evidence behind it, since no player had a single RPL game on record. Every other club had at least one returning player to reason about.

sections.heading: Season 2 — Match Day 1 (2026-09-02)
sections.html:
Beat Bucky Irving FC 2–1. 11 goals for, 6 against.

The series did not go the way the price tags suggested. LLellum opened with the best individual game of the night — 2 goals, 1 assist, 3 saves, 728 score — and then declined in every subsequent game: 728 → 395 → 319, finishing the decider with just an assist and no goals.

Sajar47 ran the exact opposite arc: 420 → 473 → 671, and finished the series as its leading scorer by total Score (1,564, ahead of even LLellum's 1,442). The half-price signing, TRS 1000, closed the series out with a 3-goal Game 3 — the first hat trick of Season 2 — and finished the day a perfect 4-for-4 on goals-to-shots.

So the $15,000 captain was outproduced by both of his cheaper teammates over the full series. That's one match day, but it's the story of this series.

The underlying numbers are less flattering than the result: Bucky Irving out-collected and out-stole them for boost, and inflicted 12 demos to Fortnite Flick's 1. They won the series while losing most of the physical battle.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• The league's only club with a title. Won the Season 1 championship with Astro, TLBoryczka and Blockymalrd, beating 999 in the Final.
  • Astro returns as captain; both title-winning teammates left. TLBoryczka went to Own Goal FC for $12,591 and Blockymalrd to Bucky Irving FC for $8,091.
  • Roster: Astro (captain, $9,269), Aowtty ($4,157), Misnfrmd ($10,317). $0 left on the cap — the only team to spend every dollar.
  • Rebuilt around the two former Fire Water Gang players who lost to them in Season 1.

sections.heading: Season 1
sections.html:
Lawson State's championship roster is the reason the Season 2 salary cap is what it is: the $23,743 cap is 110% of LS's final Season 1 roster value of $21,585.

Astro finished Season 1 as statistically the #2 player in the league — 423.26 avg points, behind only zPylo — and won the Golden Boot with 31 goals. Unlike zPylo, his team actually won the title.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
This is the most aggressive spend in the auction, and the hardest to explain from the numbers.

Misnfrmd cost $10,317 against a Season 1 Player Value of $1,000. That is a ~10× premium on the lowest-valued active player in the entire league — by far the largest gap in the draft, and not close. Aowtty cost $4,157 against $1,797, a ~2.3× premium on the second-lowest-valued active player.

Astro spent his entire cap reuniting the two Fire Water Gang players whose captain, zPylo, isn't returning for Season 2 — and paid a large premium over model for both.

The immediate consequence is visible in the current table: Lawson State has the lowest squad value in the league ($12,066), despite being the only team to spend the full cap. The model never agreed with those prices, and it still doesn't.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html:
The defending champion enters Season 2 with the biggest gap between what it spent and what the model thinks it bought. Either Astro knows something about Aowtty and Misnfrmd that a season of box scores doesn't capture, or this is the draft's most expensive misread. There is no data yet to say which — Lawson State had the Match Day 1 bye.

Worth noting fairly: Misnfrmd's Season 1 numbers came playing under a different captain on a team that didn't reach the Final. Player value is measured individually, but it isn't produced in isolation.

sections.heading: Season 2 — no games played yet
sections.html: Lawson State was on bye for Match Day 1 and has yet to play a Season 2 series.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• New club for Season 2, built by Bl4zeDaddy in his first season as a manager. He captained nothing in Season 1 — he played on 999 alongside madlabs and DrewAJC, all three of whom now manage their own clubs.
  • Roster: Bl4zeDaddy (captain, $6,736), TLBoryczka ($12,591), Spam God6450 ($3,025). $1,391 left on the cap.
  • Bought the single most expensive returning player in the draft, and the cheapest gamble available, on the same roster.

sections.heading: The draft
sections.html:
TLBoryczka at $12,591 was the 2nd-most expensive non-captain purchase of the entire auction, and a ~1.5× premium on his Season 1 model value of $8,346. Unlike most of the draft's big gaps, this one tracks: TLBoryczka finished Season 1 with the highest Player Value of any non-Champion-tier player, led the league in assists, and played more games than anyone. Paying above model for the most complete two-way player available is a legible decision.

Spam God6450 at $3,025 is the opposite kind of bet — a player with no Season 1 Player Value at all, because TTT was pulled from competition partway through the season and their values were voided. His raw numbers over 7 games (411.71 avg points) would have been 3rd-best in the league had they counted. $3,025 buys that upside with almost no downside risk.

sections.heading: What the numbers say
sections.html: The clearest "spend to win now" build in the league: one proven, expensive veteran anchoring a cheap flier and a mid-priced captain. It's the only roster where the most expensive player is demonstrably the best player, rather than the most expensive player being a question mark.

sections.heading: Season 2 — Match Day 1 (2026-09-02)
sections.html:
Swept California Gurls 3–0. 11 goals for, 5 against — the best team on the night by any measure.

The shape of the win is the interesting part. Own Goal FC recorded just 4 saves across three games, fewest of any team that played — not because the defense was bad, but because they barely needed it. They spent the least time of any team in their own defensive third (43.8%) and the most in the opponent's (22.6%). They had the ball, and the game, in the other end.

The two-man split was stark. Bl4zeDaddy scored in all three games — 3-for-3, plus 2 assists — and recorded zero saves across the entire series. Pure attack. TLBoryczka handled everything else: 4 goals, 2 assists, and 3 of the team's 4 total saves, the only OG player with a save in every game. Spam God6450's 3-goal Game 2 was the night's other standout.

One caution flag: they also led the league in time spent capped at 100 boost (529.8 seconds), which is wasted resource. Against this opponent it cost nothing.

Territorial figures are ballchasing.com proxies, not literal possession.
